Getting Started with timescapes

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

timescapes summarizes a binary condition through time. A value of 1 indicates presence and 0 indicates absence. Metric names must match a value returned by ts_list_metrics() exactly.

A binary vector

Here is a small example with two periods of the presence of some condition separated by the absence of that condition. Each time step in this case represents a year, so the first two years have the condition, then two years of absence, followed by three more years of presence and one year of absence.

library(timescapes)

x <- c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0)

The values can be visualized as a simple timeline.

plot(
  seq_along(x), x,
  type = "s",
  ylim = c(-0.1, 1.1),
  xlab = "Time step",
  ylab = "Habitat available",
  yaxt = "n",
  main = "Binary habitat availability through time"
)
axis(2, at = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"), las = 1)

Now, calculate a few metrics using ts_metric(), selecting from the available list of metrics found by using ts_list_metrics().

ts_list_metrics()
#>  [1] "total_time"      "n_periods"       "gap_mean"        "gap_max"        
#>  [5] "duration_sd"     "edge_density"    "autocorr"        "aggregation"    
#>  [9] "core_time_index" "n_core_periods"
ts_metric(x, "total_time")
#> [1] 5
ts_metric(x, "n_periods")
#> [1] 2
ts_metric(x, "gap_mean")
#> [1] 1.5

Time steps are unitless ordered observations with a duration defined by the user. Gap metrics include leading and trailing absence runs by default. Set include_boundary_gaps = FALSE to count only gaps between presence periods; no qualifying gaps returns 0, including for an all-absence series.

For core metrics, supply min_core_period, a positive whole number of time steps. A presence run qualifies when its full length is at least this threshold. core_time_index divides the total length of qualifying runs by total presence time (0 if there is no presence); n_core_periods counts qualifying runs. Omitting the threshold uses 15 time steps and issues one warning per vector or raster call. The former core_buffer argument is no longer accepted.

For example:

ts_metric(x, "core_time_index", min_core_period = 3)
#> [1] 0.6
ts_metric(x, "n_core_periods", min_core_period = 3)
#> [1] 1

Every observed value must be 0 or 1. A series containing a missing time step produces NA, because removing or reinterpreting that step could change the temporal pattern.

ts_metric(c(1, 1, NA, 0), "n_periods")
#> [1] NA

A raster time series

A terra::SpatRaster can represent the same type of series at many locations. Layers are treated as ordered time steps.

library(terra)
#> terra 1.9.50

r <- rast(nrows = 2, ncols = 2, nlyrs = 4)
values(r) <- matrix(
  c(
    1, 1, 0, 1,
    0, 0, 0, 0,
    1, 0, 1, 0,
    1, 1, 1, 1
  ),
  nrow = ncell(r),
  byrow = TRUE
)

periods <- ts_raster_metric(r, "n_periods")
values(periods)
#>      n_periods
#> [1,]         2
#> [2,]         0
#> [3,]         2
#> [4,]         1

The result is a one-layer raster with the same geometry as the input. Raster cells containing missing or non-binary values follow the same validation rules as vector inputs.

Citation

Wan, H. Y. (2025). It’s about time: Temporal fragmentation and metrics for habitat change. Landscape Ecology, 40, 226. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10980-025-02252-4
